pilot_pr.note: First paint-vm-ascii consumer; established the PaintGlyphRun-per-line pattern and the CliBuilder argv[0] convention gotcha (see lessons.md, 'C#' section).

known_gotchas: CliBuilder.Parser expects argv[0] to be a program name (C/Go convention); language's real args must be prepended with a placeholder, not passed raw.

LoadCow-equivalent file-path building from a user-supplied cowfile flag needs path-traversal / rooted-path-override protection (see cowsay.cs LoadCow for the pattern: GetFileName-only + reject rooted + verify containment).
paint-vm-ascii's glyph_run treats glyph_id as a literal Unicode code point (ASCII-backend-specific relaxation), not a font-internal glyph index -- see spec section 3.1.
Output must be verified byte-identical against an existing port (e.g. Go) for several flag combos, modulo paint-vm-ascii's spec-mandated trailing-blank-line trimming.
Gradle (java/kotlin): must redirect build output away from build/ (collides with BUILD file on case-insensitive filesystems) -- see lessons.md Gradle entries.
Swift on Windows needs the winget toolchain + vcvars setup -- see memory 'Swift on Windows setup'.
Lua rockspecs must pin immutable refs (tag/SHA), not moving branch tips -- see lessons.md Lua section.

build-tool's requiresExplicitPrereqs list (validator.go) is currently {python, typescript, perl} -- haskell is NOT in it, so cabal.project is the source of truth there (must list every transitive local package per lessons.md's Haskell section). For languages that ARE in the list, BUILD must textually reference every transitive local prerequisite's path (e.g. -I../../../packages/<lang>/<dep>/lib) -- use lib/import statements inside source files are invisible to the validator. Verify locally by building code/programs/go/build-tool and running -validate-build-files -detect-languages before pushing any language's cowsay PR; costly to discover only from a CI failure. See lessons.md 'Perl' section for the full writeup.

discovered_work.title: paint-vm-ascii's diagonal-line Bresenham loop can hang forever for some slopes
discovered_work.severity: high -- infinite loop / hang, not a crash, so it can't even be caught by a try/catch; a DoS if any caller feeds attacker-controlled line coordinates
discovered_work.details: renderLine's Bresenham loop seeds `error = 0` instead of the standard `error = deltaCol - deltaRow`. With error=0, for some (deltaRow, deltaCol) ratios (verified: deltaRow=1, deltaCol=3, e.g. a line from (0,0) to a clip-clamped target (row=1, col=3)) the `row` cursor overshoots `r2` and never returns to it, so the loop's `row == r2 && col == c2` break condition never becomes true again -- infinite loop. Confirmed by direct simulation (not just the Dart translation): the exact same `error = 0` initialization is present verbatim in code/packages/kotlin/paint-vm-ascii/src/main/kotlin/com/codingadventures/paintvmascii/PaintVmAscii.kt's renderLine, and (by inspection, same authorship pattern) very likely code/packages/java/paint-vm-ascii and code/packages/haskell/paint-vm-ascii's line-drawing too -- all three are already merged to main. Fixed in the new Dart port (this PR) by seeding `error = deltaCol - deltaRow` instead; verified against several slopes (steep, shallow, 45-degree, reversed direction) all converge correctly with the fix.
discovered_work.note: None of the merged cowsay ports currently call PaintLine (cowsay only emits PaintGlyphRun, and PaintRect for nothing that reaches this path), so this bug is dormant in production cowsay usage today -- but it's a real hang vector in a shared, already-merged package's public contract (P2D02 paint-vm-ascii) for any other/future consumer.
discovered_work.next_action: issue #12093 tracks the haskell/java/kotlin fix as separate, independent work -- not part of this loop's backlog. For swift-cowsay and lua-cowsay (both building a fresh paint-vm-ascii in this loop), seed the Bresenham error term to `deltaCol - deltaRow` from the start rather than repeating the bug a fourth/fifth time.

discovered_work.title: PR #12162 round 7: 3 more Windows BUILD_windows gaps found by build(windows-latest), after the sql-vm/mini-sqlite #12179 fix pushed
discovered_work.found_during: PR #12162 (issue #12152 fix), round 7 -- monitoring the CI run after pushing the #12179 unixepoch fix
discovered_work.details: build(windows-latest) failed with 6 package failures: python/ir-to-jvm-class-file (issue #12178, deliberately not fixed), rust/embeddable-tcp-server + rust/irc-net-reactor (known pre-existing Windows network-stack limitations, out of scope), and 3 NEW fixable gaps -- python/brainfuck-iir-compiler and python/twig-jit-wasm had no BUILD_windows at all (fell back to running BUILD verbatim under cmd.exe, hitting the forward-slash '.venv/bin/python' misparse), and python/macsyma-runtime's BUILD_windows existed but was stale -- missing 4 deps present in BUILD (cas-mnewton, cas-laplace, cas-fourier, cas-ode), causing pip to try to resolve coding-adventures-cas-fourier from PyPI instead of the local editable path. Fixed all 3: created BUILD_windows for brainfuck-iir-compiler and twig-jit-wasm (translating .venv/bin/python -> .venv\Scripts\python per the known forward-slash gotcha), and synced macsyma-runtime's BUILD_windows dep list to match BUILD. Verified all 3 locally: macsyma-runtime (499 tests, 91.06% coverage), twig-jit-wasm (23 tests, 100% coverage), brainfuck-iir-compiler (74 tests, 96.82% coverage) -- all pass with the fixed BUILD_windows install commands. Confirms the windows-build-affected-set-cascade pattern (see the PR's own commit history/notes) is still producing new-but-mechanical instances of the same 2 known root causes (missing BUILD_windows, stale/out-of-sync deps) even this late in the cascade.
discovered_work.next_action: none -- fixed and pushed as part of PR #12162 round 7. If build(windows-latest) still fails after this push, keep applying the same triage: known issues (#12178, the 2 rust network tests) vs new mechanical BUILD_windows gaps.
